Goleniow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Goleniów, Poland

Demolished. Goleniów's Jewish presence is documented from the 18th century, growing to 165 people by 1840 before beginning to emigrate abroad; only 77 remained by 1933. Following Kristallnacht, the community was imprisoned in the local Goleniów jail, then moved to Szczecin in 1940 and from there deported to Bełżec, where none survived. This cemetery, established around 1816, was likely destroyed alongside the town synagogue during Kristallnacht in November 1938 and razed after the war; remarkably, during a 2019 park revitalization project, the site was deliberately spared further disturbance after the Provincial Conservator of Monuments intervened to protect it.
